To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) hierarchical recognition processing enables a 2.5x reduction in ConvNet complexity, (2) the Envision platform is a 0.26-10TOPS/w sub-word parallel ConvNet accelerator in 28nm FD-SOI, (3) Envision achieves 2.4x better recognition rate than state-of-the-art, and 2.7x lower energy-efficiency.

We introduce a novel hierarchical recognition processing architecture and the Envision platform, a subword-parallel ConvNet processor in 28 nm FDSOI, that achieves 10 TOPS/W while maintaining recognition rate.

1) we propose a hierarchical recognition processing architecture that combines a coarse-grained recognition engine with a fine-grained recognition engine, 2) we propose a dynamic voltage-accuracy-frequency-scalable (DAFS) processing engine that can be dynamically configured for different ConvNets and different accuracy levels, 3) we demonstrate that Envision achieves 0.26-10 TOPS/W energy-efficiency, while achieving 99% accuracy on a state-of-the-art ConvNet (AlexNet),

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Envision platform enables always-on visual classification in wearable devices, with a power efficiency of 10TOPS/watt.
the Envision processor is the first energy-scalable subword-parallel Convolutional Neural network processor in the literature.
Envision is the first ConvNet accelerator that achieves 1) energy efficiencies of 10 TOPS/W (0.26-to 10 TOPS), 2) recognition rates of 95%, while 3) maintaining throughput of 1 frame/s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the first 10TOPS-Watt Convolutional Neural Net (CNN) Processor.
Envision is a hierarchical recognition processing platform for always-on visual recognition, which is enabled by a subword-parallel ConvNet processor achieving up to 10 TOPS/W.
we have developed a new architecture that is scalable in terms of voltage, accuracy and frequency, and is able to achieve 10 TOPS/W while maintaining recognition rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hierarchical recognition can be implemented in a single processor, while providing energy-scaling.
energy-efficiency of ConvNets can be improved by orders of magnitude, by exploiting the inherent parallelism in ConvNet operations, while maintaining recognition rates.
the energy-efficiency of a ConvNet accelerator is limited by its data movement requirements and that a hierarchical recognition architecture is key to achieve high efficiency.
